findings.claim: requestJsonIpc leaves an observed peer exit listener registered when the TCP/Unix socket emits an error, leaking listeners and allowing a later peer exit to destroy an already-failed request's socket.
findings.evidence: The new peer listener is registered with `peer.once("exit", onPeerExit)` and removed only inside `settle`, but the existing `socket.on("error", (error) => { ... rejectRequest(error); })` path was not changed to call `settle`; acceptance criteria explicitly asks to look for missed cleanup/listeners in IPC request liveness.
findings.suggested_fix: Route the socket error path through `settle(() => rejectRequest(error))` (or a typed `SidecarIpcError`) so timeout and peer listeners are always cleared on every terminal path.

findings.claim: A remote error response rejects without settling the IPC request, so the timeout remains armed and any peer exit listener remains registered after the promise is already rejected.
findings.evidence: In the `response.ok === false` branch the code calls `rejectRequest(new SidecarIpcError(...))` and returns, unlike timeout/close/peer-exit paths that call `settle`; this violates the focus requirement to check for listener/timer cleanup and changes behaviour for peer users.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the remote-error rejection in `settle(() => rejectRequest(new SidecarIpcError(...)))`.

findings.claim: convergeSidecarLaunch lets exceptions thrown by `onProgress` abort launch convergence despite the API comment saying the callback must not throw.
findings.evidence: The type comment added above `onProgress` says `Called on every pass of the wait; callers decide what changed. Must not throw.`, but the implementation calls `options.onProgress?.({ attempts, launcherPid: launcher.pid, phase: lastPhase });` without a try/catch; acceptance criteria requires looking for error-handling gaps in event-driven convergence.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch and ignore or trace exceptions from `onProgress` so observer bugs cannot terminate convergence.
